lines.before: The kit lives in the working folder and never in the repo by default. The kit's own `CLAUDE.md` and the personal `CLAUDE.local.md` never go public, even when the kit is tracked; a repo that owns its `CLAUDE.md` keeps it, and the kit's goes to `CLAUDE.local.md` (the overlay). The install lists every kit path, and the owner's `never` list, in a marked block of `.git/info/exclude` (never pushed, so the names stay private) and turns on the kit's git hooks. `.kit/tracking.json`: `track` names every file the owner wants in the repo (kit files chosen to show growth are added on purpose with `git add -f`); `never` names paths that must never be committed (another party's material, private notes). Every commit runs the commit check: staging a kit file not in `track`, a `never` path or a secret-shaped file or value is blocked. Committing the whole kit (`"kit": "tracked"`) is the owner's explicit choice, for a private repo only. **Limits:** git hooks run only where the kit is installed (another computer: install there first) and are skipped by `--no-verify` - a tool that uses it is a stop-and-tell-the-owner event. Why: the kit and the owner's notes are private working material; a public repo keeps every commit forever.

lines.before: Before the first push, run the strictest check once: `node .claude/first-push-check.mjs`, with the deep sweep (rule:sweep-tiers, first push). It reads every commit's whole tree (merges included) and fails on a kit path, a `never` path, or a secret-shaped file or value in ANY commit, a deleted one included; on an empty `track`, a `track` entry with no tracked file, or a wanted file that is ignored; and on a `never` file sitting unignored in the folder. It lists untracked files to decide. The owner reviews `git ls-files` against the plan. A history hit means rewriting history or a fresh repo, never "delete it in the next commit". The remote is made private first and public only after the owner checks what landed. On a pass the check records the commit; the pre-push hook lets only that commit (or its ancestors and tags) out until it is on a remote branch. **Protect main** once the repo is public and CI has a gate check: copy `.claude/kit/branch-protection.json` to `.kit/`, put the check's name in it (A26), on the owner's yes run `gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection --input .kit/branch-protection.json`, and read it back; the rule requires that one check, blocks force pushes and deletion, needs no review for a solo owner, and lets admins bypass. `/methodology-kit status` flags an unprotected main. **Every repo, private included,** turns on auto-merge and branch deletion once it exists, on the owner's yes (the gate prints the command; read back); with no required check the merge gate stays NO GO. Why: the first push sets the foundation; what it carries is public for good.
